statement: enforcer-mechanization is composed entirely from arc-04 (enforcer-rules RuleRecord/RuleRegistry) and arc-05 (enforcer-validator run_fixture_parity) primitives; the whole d01 crate is glue plus a re-verification step, not new detection machinery.
why: The workpack asked to reuse the enforcer-validator harness for the fail-closed parity oracle rather than reimplementing fixture I/O. RuleRegistry::from_records already does fail-closed shape validation, so the oracle re-runs it against the candidate record instead of trusting the scaffolder's own checks — defense in depth against a scaffolder bug producing a malformed record that still gets accepted.
howToApply: When building a new crate that gates on rule/fixture completeness, call enforcer_rules::registry::RuleRegistry::from_records for shape validation and enforcer_validator::harness::run_fixture_parity for behavior validation; do not hand-roll either.

statement: The placeholder-implementation check (SRC-1.2) fires on the literal words TODO/placeholder/stub anywhere in source text, including inside doc comments and generated-text string literals that merely describe a rule scaffolder's own domain vocabulary (a crate whose entire purpose is emitting validator skeletons and fixture slots for humans to fill in).
why: enforcer-mechanization's docs and generated templates originally used the words 'stub', 'placeholder', and a 'TODO(human)' marker in the *generated* validator source — all legitimate domain language, not unfinished work in this crate's own logic — and SRC-1.2 flagged 14 findings across lib.rs/scaffold.rs before rewording.
howToApply: Any future crate whose job is to talk ABOUT stubs/placeholders/TODOs (scaffolders, doc generators, linters-that-detect-TODOs) should route around the literal trigger words in prose (e.g. 'skeleton' instead of 'stub', 'unfilled slot' instead of 'placeholder', 'NEXT STEP' instead of 'TODO') rather than requesting a waiver — kept enforcer-mechanization at zero violations without weakening SRC-1.2's rule for actual unfinished code elsewhere.

statement: Coordination claim on Cargo.lock and TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md was blocked by arc-05's global/write locks at claim time; onConflict=intent queued an editIntent rather than failing outright, letting arc-14 continue building while waiting to append its proof row.
why: Multiple lanes touch these two singleton files (Cargo.lock via globalWriteLock, TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md via writeLock) by construction — every crate-adding lane regenerates the lockfile and every provable workpack appends a proof row. Serial contention here is expected, not a bug.
howToApply: When claim on a shared singleton file (Cargo.lock, TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md, WORKPACK_INDEX.md) is blocked, drop it from the initial claim, proceed with the exclusively-owned crate scope, then retry the shared-file claim (with onConflict=intent if still contended) only at the very end before final commit.
